exposure: double balloon catheter induction of labor
outcome: duration of first stage of labor
cohort: The study included 577 COVID-19-affected women who either underwent induction of labor with a double balloon catheter or had spontaneously started delivery.
finding: Double balloon catheter induction of labor in pregnant women with COVID-19 infection resulted in significantly shorter labor durations and was not associated with increased risks of maternal complications, fetal distress, intrapartum fever, or cesarean section compared to spontaneous delivery.
mod_finding: The use of a double balloon catheter for labor induction was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean section in COVID-19-affected women.
